# Go-Ai agent context

Go-Ai is a small OpenAI-compatible HTTP gateway for server-side applications and services. It exposes a protected chat completions endpoint, resolves local model aliases, and proxies requests to configured LLM providers. It is not an agent framework and does not execute application tools.

## API contract

- `GET /health` is public and provides simple liveness only; it does not check provider keys, upstream providers, or the model catalog.
- `POST /v1/chat/completions` requires `Authorization: Bearer <GO_AI_SHARED_SECRET>`. Send an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions JSON body; `stream: true` uses HTTP/SSE pass-through. Go-Ai resolves local aliases and proxies the upstream response.
- `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` requires bearer auth and proxies Groq-compatible multipart STT directly to Groq. `Content-Length` is mandatory: absent returns `411 content_length_required`; declared length above `GROQ_STT_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` (`25000000` bytes by default) returns `413 payload_too_large`. It streams rather than persisting or fully buffering audio; the byte cap is not an audio-duration limit.
- `POST /v1/audio/speech` requires bearer auth and proxies Groq-compatible JSON TTS requests and binary responses directly to Groq. Neither audio endpoint uses model aliases, fallback, or realtime transport.
- `GET /v1/models` requires bearer auth. It is an operator endpoint for local aliases, discovered provider catalog diagnostics, and runtime Gemini selection metadata; it is not an upstream OpenAI pass-through.
- `GET /v1/status` requires bearer auth. It is an operator endpoint for process-local runtime metrics and a compact runtime Gemini selection snapshot; values reset on restart and are not shared or persisted across instances.
- Model: omit `model` to use `default`. At startup and each `MODEL_REFRESH_INTERVAL` refresh (`1h` by default), Go-Ai strips an optional `models/` catalog prefix and selects the highest numeric stable Gemini Flash ID exactly matching `gemini-<major>.<minor>-flash` with an optional numeric revision. The exact rule excludes preview, experimental, lite, pro, image, audio, live, TTS, embedding, research, computer, and every other non-matching ID.
- Dynamic candidates: `default` tries the selected direct Gemini primary, then dynamic OpenRouter `openrouter/free` only for existing retryable fallback cases; it does not fall back for `400`, `401`, or `403`. With no eligible startup candidate, `default` uses OpenRouter only; explicit `gemini-flash` returns `503 model_unavailable`. A later Gemini catalog failure retains the active direct primary, whereas a successful Gemini catalog with no eligible ID clears it. `openrouter-free` and potentially paid `openrouter-gemini` (`google/gemini-2.5-flash`) remain static aliases.
- The runtime Gemini selection is catalog-only: it does not imply paid/chat/SSE/tool compatibility validation. It is process-local, is recomputed after restart, and has no cross-instance coordination. Target apps must keep using `default` (or omit `model`) rather than provider slugs from `/v1/models`.
- `/v1/models` and `/v1/status` expose `runtime_gemini_selection` with `active_primary`, `last_known_primary`, `last_refresh_at`, `last_selection_at`, `last_result`, `last_result_category`, and `process_local`; treat it as diagnostics, not an app routing contract.
- Successful upstream responses are proxied with their status, headers, and body.

## Integration rules for coding agents

- Call Go-Ai from server-side or backend code only.
- Do not expose `GO_AI_SHARED_SECRET` in browser code, public env vars, client bundles, logs, telemetry, or screenshots.
- Target apps usually need server-side env vars named `GO_AI_BASE_URL` and `GO_AI_SHARED_SECRET`.
- Use `POST ${GO_AI_BASE_URL}/v1/chat/completions` with `Content-Type: application/json` and bearer auth.
- For non-streaming responses, parse the JSON response after checking `response.ok`.
- For streaming, send `stream: true` and read `response.body` as a stream; do not call `res.json()` on streaming responses.
- Preserve the target app's public API/UI contract when replacing provider SDK calls.
- Tool execution, memory, and provider-specific tool validation belong to the calling app. Go-Ai only replaces the local model alias and proxies `tools`, `tool_choice`, assistant `tool_calls`, and follow-up `role: "tool"` messages.
- Preserve unknown nested assistant tool-call fields as opaque metadata and return them unchanged with matching `role: "tool"` results. Assemble streaming tool-call deltas losslessly before the next turn; Go-Ai forwards SSE bytes without parsing or rewriting them.
- Do not move product tools, database access, permissions, memory, RBAC, or business workflows into Go-Ai.
- Do not log prompts, messages, request bodies, response bodies, tool arguments, tool results, opaque metadata, provider keys, bearer tokens, `GO_AI_SHARED_SECRET`, or `.env` values.
- For browser STT UI, enforce exactly a 5:00 maximum capture: warn at 4:30, forcibly stop and immediately upload at 5:00. This frontend control is bypassable and must not be described as a server-side duration check. Keep Go-Ai's independent byte cap, stream raw multipart via the app backend with `Content-Type` and `Content-Length`, and do not persist or fully buffer audio.
- TTS is app-owned UX, not an automatic Go-Ai feature. In a `ru` UI, hide or disable the TTS control and never call `/v1/audio/speech`. In an `en` UI, call TTS only when an app-owned reliable language guard has confirmed the final response text is English; UI locale alone is insufficient. Keep non-English or indeterminate text as text, with no automatic translation and no promise of Russian TTS. STT remains independent and may be used in `ru` and `en` under its documented contract, without unverified quality claims.
